Coerce a list to keyvalue object

as.keyvalue.list.Rd

x should be a list with properties descrobed in section "Details".

# S3 method for list
as.keyvalue(x, ...)

Arguments

x

a list with properties described in the details section.
...

further arguments passed to as.keyvalue.

Value

The function returns an object of class keyvalue (and list.

Details

  • All names of the list elements should be unique.

  • All elements of the list should be named.

  • All keys should be unique (a key should only be mappad to one value).

  • All elements of the list should be atomic vectors.

See also

as.keyvalue

Examples


ex <- list(
 fruit  = c("banana", "orange", "kiwi"),
 car    = c("SAAB", "Volvo", "taxi", "truck"),
 animal = c("elefant")
)
as.keyvalue(ex)
#>       key  value
#> 1  banana  fruit
#> 8 elefant animal
#> 3    kiwi  fruit
#> 2  orange  fruit
#> 4    SAAB    car
#> 6    taxi    car
#> 7   truck    car
#> 5   Volvo    car
is.keyvalue(ex)
#> [1] FALSE


# An invalid list (non unique names; not because of silly classification)
ex2 <- list(
 fruit  = c("banana", "orange", "kiwi"),
 car    = c("SAAB", "Volvo", "taxi", "truck"),
 animal = c("elefant"),
 fruit  = c("President_Obama")
)
as.keyvalue(ex2)
#> Error in as.keyvalue.list(ex2): All list element names must be unique!

# An invalid list (non unique keys; kiwi appear twice)
ex3 <- list(
 fruit  = c("banana", "orange", "kiwi"),
 car    = c("SAAB", "Volvo", "taxi", "truck"),
 animal = c("elefant", "kiwi")
)
as.keyvalue(ex3)
#> Error in as.keyvalue.list(ex3): Some key(s) have duplicates! A key should only be mapped to one value (be found in one element of the list)
